intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Explore the stunning Phi Phi archipelago by longtail boat, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters at Maya Bay, visiting Monkey Beach, and discovering hidden lagoons. A full-day guided tour covering multiple islands with snorkeling gear included.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Market Tour
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene at Yaowarat Road (Chinatown), sampling pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh seafood. Join a guided walking food tour or explore independently through the bustling night stalls.

experiences.name: Similan Islands Liveaboard Snorkeling Trip
experiences.description: Embark on an overnight or day-trip liveaboard to the world-renowned Similan Islands, considered one of Asia's top snorkeling and diving destinations. Swim alongside whale sharks, manta rays, and vibrant coral reefs in protected national park waters.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta Beach Hopping by Scooter
experiences.description: Rent a scooter and independently explore Koh Lanta's diverse beaches in a single day — from the lively Long Beach to the secluded Bamboo Bay and the laid-back Kantiang Bay. Stop at local beachside shacks for fresh grilled fish and Som Tum papaya salad.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Sunday Walking Street Food & Culture Experience
experiences.description: Stroll through Chiang Mai's famous Sunday Night Market along Wualai Road, tasting northern Thai specialties like Khao Soi curry noodles, Sai Oua sausage, and Khanom Krok coconut pancakes while browsing handmade crafts and watching traditional Lanna cultural performances.
experiences.location: Wualai Road, Old City, Chiang Mai

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Phuket or Krabi Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency at the airport (look for SuperRich or airport exchange booths for better rates). Take a shared minivan or local bus to the pier, then catch a public ferry to Phi Phi Islands (Don). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a slow walk along Tonsai Village to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Tonsai Village night market. Explore the lively beachfront strip, grab a fresh fruit shake from a street cart, and watch the sunset from Tonsai Bay viewpoint. Settle in early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during your layover
meals.lunch: Grab a quick pad thai or mango sticky rice from a street stall near the pier (≈60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Tonsai Village night market — try a plate of khao pad (fried rice) or som tum (papaya salad) for 60–100 THB from local vendors

day_by_day.notes: Budget tip: Book the ferry in advance online to save time. Public ferries cost around 150–200 THB vs. private speedboats at 600+ THB. Keep small bills handy for street food.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–40 THB entry). The panoramic view of both Tonsai and Loh Dalum Bays is stunning and best enjoyed in the cooler morning hours. The hike takes about 20–30 minutes each way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Loh Dalum Beach for swimming and relaxing on the white sand. Rent a snorkel set from a local shop (≈100 THB/hour) and explore the shallow reef just off the beach. Walk over to the quieter Tonsai Bay side to people-watch and explore local shops.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget-friendly long-tail boat sunset cruise around Phi Phi Don (group tours ≈300–400 THB). Return to Tonsai Village for dinner and enjoy the lively beach bar atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or street stall near Tonsai Village — roti with banana and condensed milk (40–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach-side food shack at Loh Dalum — grilled fish with rice or noodle soup (80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant or similar local eatery in Tonsai Village — massaman curry with rice (120–150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: October is the tail end of the wet season in the Andaman — mornings are often clear but afternoon showers are possible. Carry a small rain poncho. The viewpoint hike can be muddy, wear grip shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early long-tail boat to Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh (the famous 'The Beach' location). Entry fee applies (≈400 THB). Arrive early (before 9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Snorkel around the bay and explore the limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping around Phi Phi Leh — visit Pileh Lagoon (stunning emerald water enclosed by cliffs) and Viking Cave. Most long-tail boat tours cover all these spots for 500–800 THB per person in a shared group.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Rest and shower, then head out for a beachfront fire show performance (free to watch at Tonsai beachfront bars in the evening). Enjoy a cold Chang beer (60–80 THB) while watching the show.

meals.breakfast: Street-side stall near the pier — fried egg on rice or congee (40–60 THB). Eat before boarding the boat.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks and water for the boat trip (buy from 7-Eleven the night before — very budget-friendly). Some tours include a basic lunch stop.
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant in Tonsai — green curry with jasmine rice and a fresh coconut (100–150 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor hours and a cap on tourists to protect the ecosystem. Book your long-tail boat the evening before. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, water, and a dry bag for your phone and valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak from the beach (150–200 THB/hour) and paddle around the coastline of Phi Phi Don, exploring hidden coves and rock formations at your own pace. Head toward Monkey Beach for a close-up view (stay in your kayak — the monkeys can be aggressive on land).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the public ferry from Phi Phi Don to Krabi Town (≈150–200 THB, 1.5–2 hours). Check out the famous Krabi Town Weekend Night Market if timing aligns, or explore the charming riverside town. Visit the quirky 'Krabi Walking Street' area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's Chao Fa Night Market — one of the best budget food spots in the region. Try multiple dishes from different stalls for a full meal under 150 THB.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast on Phi Phi — coconut pancake from a street cart (30–50 THB)
meals.lunch: Eat on the ferry or grab something quick at the Krabi pier — noodle soup or spring rolls (60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Chao Fa Night Market, Krabi Town — pad see ew, mango sticky rice, fresh-squeezed juice (total ≈100–150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: If staying in Krabi Town tonight, budget guesthouses near the riverside cost 300–500 THB/night. Alternatively, day-trip to Krabi and return to Phi Phi on the last ferry (check schedule — usually last ferry around 17:00–18:00).

day_by_day.morning: Head to Railay Beach from Krabi Town or Ao Nang by long-tail boat (100–150 THB each way — accessible only by boat due to limestone cliffs). Explore Railay West Beach, one of Thailand's most beautiful stretches of sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through the jungle trail to Railay East and then to the Phra Nang Cave Beach — home to a sacred princess shrine and stunning rock formations. Snorkel off Phra Nang Beach. Attempt the challenging rock-climbing trail up to the Railay Viewpoint (free, but steep).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the long-tail boat back to Ao Nang before dark. Explore Ao Nang's beachfront promenade and street food scene. Watch the sunset over the limestone karsts from Ao Nang Beach.

meals.breakfast: Ao Nang or Krabi Town street stall — khao tom (rice porridge) with egg (50–70 THB)
meals.lunch: Beach shack at Railay West — grilled corn, fresh coconut, and a simple rice dish (100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang Night Market or beachfront food stalls — tom yum soup, grilled skewers, fresh fruit (120–160 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is one of the most scenic spots in all of Thailand — worth the boat fare. October may bring some waves so confirm long-tail service is running. Wear water shoes as the boat landing at Railay East can be muddy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a shared songthaew (red truck taxi, ≈50–80 THB) from Ao Nang toward the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) near Krabi Town. Climb the famous 1,237 steps to the summit for a breathtaking 360-degree view over Krabi Province. Best done in the morning before the heat peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Krabi Town and visit the Krabi Town Pier area. Take a short longtail boat ride to see the Four Islands from a distance or simply relax at a riverside café. Visit the local fresh market near the pier to sample tropical fruits.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation. If still based in Phi Phi, catch the afternoon ferry back. Spend the evening at the Phi Phi beachfront — try a traditional Thai massage on the beach (200–300 THB/hour) and enjoy a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: 7-Eleven or local bakery near your guesthouse — toasted sandwich and Thai iced tea (40–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Riverside restaurant in Krabi Town — pad kra pao (basil stir-fry with egg on rice), a classic local favorite (80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront food stall on Phi Phi or Krabi — seafood BBQ platter shared between travelers (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is intense — bring at least 1.5L of water, wear sunscreen, and start no later than 8:00 AM. Monkeys live at the base of the temple — secure your bags. Entry is free.

day_by_day.morning: Full day Four Islands Tour departing from Krabi or Ao Nang. Islands visited typically include Koh Mor, Koh Chuak, Koh Mah, and Koh Waen. Group tours by longtail boat cost around 500–700 THB per person and include snorkeling stops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands tour — snorkel at coral reefs, explore a sandbar that appears at low tide, and relax on secluded beaches. The tour usually returns by 16:00–17:00.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening back at base. Visit a local pharmacy if you need any supplies (very affordable in Thailand). Treat yourself to a budget Thai dessert — tub tim grob (water chestnuts in coconut milk) from a street cart (30–40 THB).

meals.breakfast: Street stall near the pier — roti with egg and curry dipping sauce (50–70 THB)
meals.lunch: Included in most Four Islands tours (simple rice and fish on a beach). If not included, pack snacks from 7-Eleven.
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near accommodation — whole grilled fish with steamed rice and morning glory stir-fry (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Four Islands tour the evening before through your guesthouse or a local tour operator — avoid the first price quoted and negotiate politely. October seas may be slightly choppy — take seasickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the ferry from Phi Phi or Krabi to Koh Lanta (≈200–300 THB, 1.5–2 hours). Check into a budget bungalow on Koh Lanta (500–800 THB/night for beachfront options). Drop your bags and head straight to Long Beach (Phra Ae Beach) — one of Koh Lanta's most beautiful stretches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (150–200 THB/day) and explore Koh Lanta's coastline. Drive south toward Klong Nin Beach and Kantiang Bay — quieter and less developed. Stop at the Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) on the east coast — a charming wooden stilt village with sea gypsy heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Kantiang Bay or Klong Nin Beach — some of the best sunsets in southern Thailand. Return to Long Beach area for dinner and a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — pier-side food stall (40–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town — fresh seafood noodles or fried rice (80–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — BBQ seafood or Thai curry with coconut rice (150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less crowded than Phi Phi — a great contrast. Scooter rental is the best way to explore. Always wear a helmet and carry your passport copy. Check ferry schedules in advance as October services may be reduced.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of Koh Lanta (entry ≈200 THB). Explore jungle trails, a lighthouse with panoramic views, and pristine beaches. Spot wildlife including monitor lizards and hornbills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Koh Lanta's best snorkeling spot — Koh Rok (accessible via day trip, ≈800–1,000 THB including boat and national park fee) or snorkel directly off the beach at Kantiang Bay for free. Alternatively, visit the Tham Mai Kaeo Caves on Koh Lanta (guided cave tour ≈200 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Long Beach area. Browse the relaxed beachfront bars and restaurants. Enjoy a traditional Thai herbal steam bath or massage at a local spa (200–300 THB for a 1-hour traditional massage).

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast or nearby café — banana pancake and fresh fruit smoothie (60–90 THB)
meals.lunch: National Park café or packed lunch from 7-Eleven
meals.dinner: Night market or local Thai restaurant — pad thai, spring rolls, and fresh coconut (120–160 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok is only accessible by speedboat and conditions in October may be rough — check with local operators the morning of. The cave tour requires a local guide and a torch — book through your guesthouse.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning swim and yoga on the beach (many budget guesthouses on Koh Lanta offer free or donation-based morning yoga). Pack up and take the ferry to Koh Phi Phi or head toward Phuket (≈400–600 THB). If heading to Phuket, arrive midday and check into a budget hostel in Patong or Old Phuket Town (300–600 THB/night for dorms or basic rooms).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Phuket Old Town — vibrant Sino-Portuguese architecture, colorful street art murals, and independent boutique shops. Walk along Thalang Road and Soi Rommanee. Visit the Blue Elephant Cooking School area (just to look — dining there is expensive, but the building is beautiful and free to photograph).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the famous Sunday Walking Street Market in Phuket Old Town if it's a Sunday, or the Chillva Market (open Thursday–Sunday) for budget street food and local handicrafts.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast on Koh Lanta — beachside café with toast, eggs, and coffee (60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Phuket Old Town local kopitiam (coffee shop) — dim sum, steamed buns, and Thai iced coffee (60–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Chillva Market or local night market — wide variety of street food, aim for 100–150 THB for a full meal

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is very walkable and free to explore. Budget accommodation is best found in Old Town rather than Patong (which is more expensive and touristy). Use Grab app for affordable tuk-tuk/taxi alternatives.

day_by_day.morning: Take a shared songthaew (40 THB) to Kata or Karon Beach — less crowded and more scenic than Patong. Swim and relax on the beach. Walk the coastal path between Kata Noi and Kata Yai for beautiful views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Big Buddha (Phra Puttamingmongkol Akenakkiri) on Nakkerd Hill — free entry, one of Phuket's most iconic landmarks with panoramic island views. Nearby, visit Wat Chalong (the largest and most important Buddhist temple in Phuket — free entry).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Patong Beach for the evening if you want to experience the famous (or infamous) nightlife scene — it's free to walk around and people-watch. Alternatively, enjoy a quieter evening in Old Town with dinner and a sunset rooftop view.

meals.breakfast: Local market near your hostel — khao man gai (poached chicken on rice) or jok (congee) (50–70 THB)
meals.lunch: Street food near Kata Beach — grilled satay skewers, mango salad, fresh coconut (100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Local restaurant near Wat Chalong or Old Town — gaeng keow wan (green curry) with roti (120–160 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly when visiting Wat Chalong and the Big Buddha (cover shoulders and knees — sarongs available to borrow for free at the entrance). Songthaews run fixed routes — confirm the destination before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Phang Nga Bay — famous for its dramatic limestone karsts rising from emerald water, including the iconic James Bond Island (Khao Tapu). Book a budget group tour (600–900 THB) that includes longtail boat, kayaking through sea caves, and a visit to the floating Muslim village of Koh Panyee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Phang Nga Bay tour — kayak through mangrove tunnels and hidden lagoons. Visit Koh Panyee floating village for lunch and explore the stilt community. Return to Phuket by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final full evening in Phuket. Visit the Phuket Weekend Market (Naka Market) if open for last-minute souvenir shopping on a budget. Enjoy a farewell street food feast — try all the dishes you haven't tried yet.

meals.breakfast: Hostel or guesthouse — simple bread, fruit, and coffee before the early tour departure
meals.lunch: Koh Panyee floating village — fresh seafood rice dishes (usually included in tour or available for 100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Phuket street food final feast — pad thai, mango sticky rice, fresh-squeezed OJ, and grilled pork skewers (150–200 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Phang Nga Bay tour the day before through your hostel or a local agency. October weather may affect sea conditions — tours typically still run but confirm the morning of. This is one of the most spectacular day trips in all of Thailand — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand. Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a slow breakfast in Phuket Old Town. Visit any last sights — the Phuket Trickeye Museum (200 THB) or simply wander the colorful streets one last time. Pick up last-minute souvenirs from local markets (avoid airport shops — much more expensive).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Phuket International Airport with plenty of time. Use Grab app or pre-booked airport transfer (150–300 THB by songthaew/shared van). Check in, clear security, and enjoy your final Thai meal at the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days of island hopping, street food adventures, and beach bliss across one of the world's most stunning coastal destinations.

meals.breakfast: Old Town café — final khao tom or roti with curry, and a strong Thai iced coffee (60–90 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport food court — more expensive than street food but still affordable by Western standards (150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport snacks

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tip: Daily spending on this itinerary averages 800–1,200 THB/day (≈$22–$35 USD) excluding accommodation and inter-island transport. Keep a buffer of 2,000–3,000 THB for unexpected costs. Exchange leftover baht at the airport or keep for your next trip — Thai baht is easy to exchange globally.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and collect luggage. Take an airport transfer to Krabi or Ao Nang pier, then board a speedboat or ferry to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll along the Tonsai Village beachfront to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village walking street. Browse local shops, watch fire shows on the beach, and soak in the vibrant island atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick bite at the airport — try a Thai snack stall inside the terminal
meals.lunch: Grab a quick meal at the airport or pier — look for a pad thai or khao man gai stall
meals.dinner: Dinner at Papaya Restaurant on Phi Phi — a well-loved mid-range spot serving authentic Thai dishes like massaman curry and tom yum soup (approx. 200–350 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry transfer in advance as afternoon boats can fill up. Arrive at the pier at least 30 minutes early. Keep some cash handy as ATMs on Phi Phi charge higher fees.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided snorkeling tour around Phi Phi's iconic Maya Bay (from The Beach fame), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. Depart around 8:00 AM to beat the crowds. Snorkel gear is typically included in tour packages (approx. 800–1,200 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the island by early afternoon. Hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint — a 20-minute uphill trek rewarded with a breathtaking panoramic view of the twin bays. Cool down with a fresh coconut at the top.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Tonsai Bay beachfront for sunset cocktails. Enjoy the golden hour with a Chang beer or a fruit smoothie from one of the beach bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — try a Thai-style breakfast of jok (rice porridge) or toast with condensed milk and eggs
meals.lunch: Pack a light snack for the boat tour, or eat at a small beachside shack on Maya Bay area — fresh fruit, sandwiches, or spring rolls
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant on Phi Phi — a popular mid-range spot with excellent Thai and international fusion dishes (approx. 250–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor hours and a timed entry system to protect the ecosystem. Confirm current regulations with your tour operator. Wear reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a kayak or join a guided kayaking tour around Phi Phi Leh's limestone cliffs and hidden lagoons. Paddle through sea caves and discover secluded coves only accessible by small watercraft (approx. 400–700 THB for kayak rental).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Long Beach (Hat Yao) on Phi Phi Don — a quieter, less crowded stretch of white sand with crystal-clear water. Swim, sunbathe, and unwind. Long Beach is accessible by a short longtail boat ride or a 30-minute walk.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tonsai Village for an evening of street food exploration along the night market stalls near the pier area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery café near your hotel — try banana pancakes or fresh fruit bowls, a backpacker staple beloved by all
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Long Beach — simple grilled fish or som tum (papaya salad) from a small beach vendor (approx. 100–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at Tonsai Village night stalls — try moo ping (grilled pork skewers), pad see ew noodles, and mango sticky rice for dessert (approx. 150–250 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: October is shoulder season — occasional rain showers are possible. Carry a light rain jacket. Sea conditions are generally good but check with locals each morning.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early longtail boat to Bamboo Island (Koh Phai) — a tiny uninhabited island about 20 minutes north of Phi Phi Don, known for its stunning white sand beach and excellent snorkeling reef. Arrive early for solitude (longtail boat approx. 1,500–2,000 THB shared or join a group tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue island hopping to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for more snorkeling — known for its colorful coral and abundant marine life including clownfish and sea turtles. Return to Phi Phi by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Thai massage at one of Phi Phi's reputable massage parlors near the village — a perfect way to relax after a day on the water (approx. 300–500 THB for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your hotel before departure — request a packed breakfast or grab something quick at the pier
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or buy from the boat tour — fresh fruit, sandwiches, and bottled water; some tours include a simple lunch onboard
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Cove Restaurant — a mid-range beachfront restaurant on Phi Phi with great seafood platters and Thai curries (approx. 300–500 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring plenty of water, sunscreen, and a dry bag for your electronics. Bamboo Island has no facilities, so pack everything you need. Negotiate boat prices the evening before for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry from Phi Phi to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours, 300–400 THB). Check in to a mid-range guesthouse in Krabi Town or Ao Nang area. Visit the famous Krabi Town Weekend Market (note: if not a weekend, visit the local fresh market instead) for a taste of authentic local life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — climb the 1,237 steps to the summit for a stunning 360-degree view over Krabi's karst landscape. The climb takes about 45 minutes and is well worth the effort (free entry, small donation appreciated).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's riverside night market (Chao Fa Night Market) along the waterfront — one of Thailand's most authentic local night markets with excellent street food at very affordable prices.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near Phi Phi pier before boarding the ferry — try khanom krok (coconut rice pancakes) or a simple Thai breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch in Krabi Town at a local restaurant — try khao soi (northern Thai curry noodle soup) or a simple rice dish with multiple curries (approx. 80–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chao Fa Night Market — grilled seafood, pad thai, green curry, and fresh fruit shakes; budget 150–300 THB for a generous spread

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes, bring water, and avoid midday heat. Dress modestly as it is a sacred Buddhist site (cover shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day Four Islands Tour from Ao Nang or Krabi Town — visit Koh Mor, Koh Chuak, Koh Tub, and the famous Chicken Island (Koh Kai). Snorkel, swim, and walk across the sandbar connecting islands at low tide (tour approx. 800–1,200 THB including lunch).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Four Islands Tour — afternoon snorkeling at Koh Chuak's reef. Return to Ao Nang by late afternoon. Stroll along Ao Nang beach and browse the beachfront shops.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset at Ao Nang Beach, then head to the bustling Ao Nang Walking Street for evening entertainment, live music, and more street food.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a nearby café in Krabi — try a Thai omelette over rice or fresh fruit smoothie bowl
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the Four Islands Tour — typically a simple Thai buffet served on a beach or aboard the boat
meals.dinner: Dinner at Last Fisherman Bar & Restaurant in Ao Nang — a beloved mid-range spot with fresh seafood and great views (approx. 250–450 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: The sandbar walk between islands is tide-dependent — confirm timing with your tour operator. Bring waterproof camera or an underwater phone case for snorkeling shots.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach — one of Thailand's most beautiful and only accessible by boat. Explore East Railay and West Railay beaches, and visit the famous Princess Cave (Phra Nang Cave) with its stunning stalactites and offerings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing at Railay — the area is world-renowned for its beginner-friendly limestone walls with spectacular views. Half-day guided climbing sessions available (approx. 800–1,500 THB including instruction and gear). Alternatively, kayak through the mangroves on the eastern side.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang by longtail boat before dark (last boats typically depart around 6 PM). Enjoy a relaxed evening with dinner and a stroll along the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Ao Nang before heading to the pier — try roti with banana and condensed milk, a Thai street food classic
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant on Railay — fresh seafood or Thai curries with a view (approx. 200–350 THB); slightly pricier than mainland due to boat transport costs
meals.dinner: Dinner at Krua Thara Restaurant in Ao Nang — excellent authentic Thai cuisine at mid-range prices with a local atmosphere (approx. 200–350 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Railay is only accessible by longtail boat from Ao Nang pier (approx. 100 THB per person each way, or 300 THB to charter). Boats run frequently throughout the day. Wear water shoes as the entry to East Railay can be muddy.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry or minivan-ferry combination (approx. 2–3 hours, 350–500 THB). Check into a mid-range beachfront bungalow or guesthouse on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) — Koh Lanta's most popular and accessible beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) — a charming historic fishing village on stilts over the water with colorful Sino-Portuguese shophouses, local craft shops, and a laid-back atmosphere. Walk the wooden boardwalk and chat with friendly locals.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Long Beach — one of Koh Lanta's finest sunset spots. Watch the sky turn orange and pink over the Andaman Sea from the beach.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi guesthouse or grab a quick bite near the pier — fried rice or a simple noodle soup
meals.lunch: Lunch in Koh Lanta Old Town — try a local restaurant serving fresh seafood and southern Thai dishes like kaeng tai pla (fish kidney curry) (approx. 100–200 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — fresh grilled fish, tom kha soup, and sticky rice with mango (approx. 250–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules to Koh Lanta vary by season — book tickets the day before. October may see some rain but Koh Lanta is generally sheltered from the worst weather. The island has a very relaxed pace — embrace the slower rhythm.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore Koh Lanta's southern end — visit Koh Lanta National Park (approx. 200 THB entry). Trek through jungle trails to a lighthouse with panoramic views, and snorkel at the park's pristine beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kantiang Bay (Hat Kantiang) — considered one of Koh Lanta's most beautiful and secluded beaches. Swim in the calm waters and relax on the nearly empty beach. Continue to Klong Nin Beach for more exploration.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your accommodation area. Enjoy a traditional Thai cooking class if available locally (approx. 1,000–1,500 THB) — learn to make 3–4 dishes including a curry paste from scratch.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a beachside café near your guesthouse — try American-style breakfast or Thai-style with rice soup and pickled vegetables
meals.lunch: Lunch at a small local restaurant near Kantiang Bay — simple and fresh; try pla kapong neung manao (steamed fish with lime and chili) (approx. 150–250 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Drunken Sailors Bar & Restaurant on Koh Lanta — a popular mid-range spot with great cocktails and Thai-Western fusion food (approx. 250–400 THB per person)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental costs approx. 200–300 THB per day. Roads in the south can be rough — drive carefully, especially after rain. Always wear a helmet and carry your international driving permit.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day snorkeling trip to the Koh Haa (Five Islands) archipelago — one of the best snorkeling and diving sites in the Andaman Sea, with stunning underwater caves, tunnels, and diverse marine life (tour approx. 1,200–1,800 THB including lunch and gear).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Koh Haa tour — afternoon snorkeling at a second site. Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Relax at the beach or get a seaside massage.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the night market in Ban Saladan (Koh Lanta's main town near the ferry pier) — a small but authentic market with local street food and fresh produce.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse before the early tour departure — or grab something quick at a café near the pier
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the Koh Haa tour — typically a Thai lunch served on the boat or a nearby beach
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ban Saladan night market — fresh seafood, satay, papaya salad, and Thai iced tea (approx. 150–250 THB for a full spread)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Haa is a protected marine area — no touching coral and reef-safe sunscreen is mandatory. Visibility is typically excellent (15–20 meters) making it ideal for underwater photography.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Koh Lanta back to Krabi, then take an airport transfer or bus to Phuket (approx. 3–4 hours total journey). Check into a mid-range hotel in Patong, Kata, or Karon Beach area — each offers a different vibe from lively to relaxed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Kata Beach or Karon Beach — both are beautiful, well-maintained beaches with calmer waters than Patong. Swim, rent a beach chair (approx. 100 THB), and enjoy the classic Phuket beach experience.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Patong's famous Bangla Road for a lively evening out — enjoy the street performances, night market stalls, and the electric atmosphere of Phuket's most famous entertainment strip.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Koh Lanta guesthouse before checkout — or grab food at the pier
meals.lunch: Lunch at a restaurant in Krabi or along the road — try a simple rice dish or noodle soup at a roadside restaurant (approx. 80–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a street food stall on or near Bangla Road — try grilled corn, pad thai, and fresh fruit skewers; alternatively dine at a sit-down restaurant nearby (approx. 200–350 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Phuket is larger and more developed than the islands — traffic can be heavy, especially in the Patong area. Consider staying in Kata or Karon for a slightly quieter experience while still being close to Patong.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Phuket Old Town — a UNESCO-recognized area with beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture, vibrant street art, and excellent local cafés. Walk along Thalang Road, Dibuk Road, and Soi Romanee. Visit the Phuket Thai Hua Museum for cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a speedboat or join a tour to Phang Nga Bay — visit the famous James Bond Island (Khao Phing Kan), paddle through sea caves by kayak, and marvel at the towering limestone karsts rising from emerald water (tour approx. 1,500–2,000 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket for your final evening on the island. Visit the Malin Plaza Night Market in Patong or the Chillva Market near Phuket Town for excellent street food and local shopping.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Phuket Old Town — try the famous Kopitiam by Wilai for authentic Phuket-style breakfast with local coffee and dim sum (approx. 150–250 THB)
meals.lunch: Lunch included in the Phang Nga Bay tour — typically a seafood lunch at a floating village restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chillva Market — a hip outdoor market with excellent street food, craft beer, and live music; budget 200–350 THB for a satisfying meal and drinks

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot in the early morning before it gets hot. Phang Nga Bay tours book up quickly — reserve in advance. The bay is most beautiful in morning light.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Phuket — visit Big Buddha (Phra Phutthamingmongkol Akenakkiri) on Nakkerd Hill for panoramic views over the island and a peaceful spiritual experience. The 45-meter white marble statue is one of Phuket's most iconic landmarks (free entry, donations welcome).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kata Noi Beach — one of Phuket's most picturesque and less crowded beaches — for a final swim and relaxation session. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at a nearby shop. Transfer to Phuket International Airport for your departure flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket International Airport. Arrive 2–3 hours before your flight. Browse duty-free shops for Thai snacks, silk products, and elephant-themed gifts to bring home.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast at a local café near your hotel — try khao tom (rice soup) with crispy garlic and ginger, a comforting Thai morning staple
meals.lunch: Lunch near Kata Noi Beach — a relaxed beachside meal of fresh seafood or a Thai green curry (approx. 200–350 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at the airport — Phuket International Airport has decent food court options with Thai dishes at reasonable prices (approx. 150–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Confirm your flight time and any transit connections. Pack reef-safe sunscreen and any liquid items in checked luggage to avoid confiscation at security.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at destination airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from the airport to Rassada Pier, Phuket, followed by a luxury speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique stay, unwind on the private terrace, and enjoy a welcome coconut drink while soaking in the panoramic Andaman Sea views
day_by_day.evening: Sunset stroll along Phi Phi Don's Tonsai Village waterfront. Explore the vibrant night market lanterns and sample local street snacks — grilled satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and fresh coconut ice cream from the beachside vendors

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: N/A — traveling; grab a light snack at Phuket International Airport's premium lounge
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi Don — a beloved island institution serving authentic Thai curries and fresh seafood; try the massaman curry with tiger prawns

day_by_day.notes: Arrange your private speedboat transfer in advance. October marks the tail end of the monsoon season — seas are generally calm but carry a light rain jacket. Check in is typically 14:00; request early luggage drop if arriving before room is ready.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat sunrise tour departing at 06:30 to Maya Bay (The Beach) before the daily crowds arrive. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise lagoon, snorkel among vibrant coral gardens, and photograph the iconic limestone cliffs bathed in golden morning light
day_by_day.afternoon: Island hopping by private speedboat to Phi Phi Leh's Pileh Lagoon and Viking Cave. Enjoy a premium packed lunch on the boat with fresh fruit, sandwiches, and chilled beverages. Snorkel at Shark Point and spot blacktip reef sharks in their natural habitat
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner cocktails at Reggae Bar's rooftop overlooking the bay, then a leisurely walk through Tonsai Village's street food alley — sample pad thai cooked fresh to order, deep-fried spring rolls, and grilled corn with chili butter

meals.breakfast: Full Thai breakfast at your boutique hotel — jasmine rice congee, fresh tropical fruit platter, and Thai-style omelets with herbs
meals.lunch: Premium in-boat picnic lunch curated by your hotel — fresh baguette sandwiches, local fruits, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Papaya Restaurant, Phi Phi Don — renowned for its fresh catch of the day, whole steamed fish with lime and garlic, and authentic green papaya salad

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has regulated visitor hours and a conservation fee applies. Book your private longtail boat the evening before through your hotel concierge for the best early access slot.

day_by_day.morning: Guided hike to Phi Phi Don's iconic ViewPoint for panoramic 360-degree views of both Tonsai and Loh Dalum bays. The 30-minute trek through jungle paths is rewarded with one of Thailand's most photographed vistas — best captured in the soft morning light
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking adventure through the hidden sea caves and mangrove channels on the quieter eastern side of Phi Phi Don. A private guide leads you through emerald-green lagoons and secret coves accessible only by kayak at certain tide levels
day_by_day.evening: Beachside dining experience on Loh Dalum Beach under the stars. Many restaurants set tables directly on the sand with tiki torches and candle lighting for a romantic atmosphere

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel — avocado toast with chili flakes, fresh-pressed watermelon juice, and Thai-style eggs with holy basil
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Chill Bar & Restaurant on Loh Dalum Beach — fresh seafood platters, coconut-based soups, and cold Chang beer or fresh lime soda
meals.dinner: Phi Phi Banyan Villa Restaurant — upscale garden dining with a curated menu of Thai and Mediterranean fusion; signature dish is the grilled lobster with lemongrass butter sauce

day_by_day.notes: The ViewPoint hike can be slippery after rain — wear proper footwear. Start the hike by 07:00 to avoid midday heat and capture the best light. Kayak tours should be booked through your hotel for vetted guides.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat day trip to Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai), a pristine uninhabited island with powder-white sand and shallow reefs. Arrive early for exclusive beach time before day-trippers arrive — swim, snorkel, and relax in complete serenity
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for world-class snorkeling in crystal-clear waters teeming with clownfish, parrotfish, and sea turtles. Your private boat captain ensures you visit the best spots based on current conditions
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don by late afternoon. Freshen up at the hotel and head to Tonsai Pier area for a street food evening — explore the night market for grilled squid on skewers, pad see ew noodles, and fresh mango with sticky rice

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the hotel — croissants, local honey, tropical fruit, and barista-prepared coffee
meals.lunch: Freshly grilled seafood BBQ on Bamboo Island beach, prepared by your private boat crew — whole fish, tiger prawns, and corn on the cob with Thai dipping sauces
meals.dinner: Pee Pee Bakery & Restaurant — a local favorite for its authentic Thai street food atmosphere; order the tom yum kung (spicy shrimp soup) and pad kra pao (holy basil stir-fry)

day_by_day.notes: Bamboo Island is a national park — entry fees apply. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a reusable water bottle, and underwater camera. Your hotel can pack a premium cooler with drinks and snacks for the boat trip.

day_by_day.morning: Luxurious morning at leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast, a dip in the hotel pool, and a 60-minute traditional Thai massage at your boutique stay's in-house spa or a nearby wellness center. The aromatic herbal compress treatment is highly recommended
day_by_day.afternoon: Private longtail boat transfer to Phi Phi Leh for a private snorkeling session at Loh Samah Bay. The bay's shallow, calm waters make it ideal for spotting colorful reef fish and soft corals. Followed by relaxation time on the secluded beach
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class experience at a local Phi Phi culinary studio — learn to prepare three classic Thai dishes: tom kha gai (coconut chicken soup), green curry from scratch, and mango sticky rice. Enjoy your creations as dinner

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — full Thai set with rice soup, steamed jasmine rice, fried egg, and fresh papaya
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Phi Phi Leh — your boat captain brings a premium bento-style meal with sushi rolls, fresh fruit, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the cooking class — dine in the studio garden setting with fellow travelers and a glass of Thai rice wine or cold Singha beer

day_by_day.notes: Book the Thai cooking class at least two days in advance through your hotel. The spa massage is best scheduled in the morning to enhance relaxation before afternoon activities. Bring a waterproof bag for Phi Phi Leh snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phi Phi Islands by premium speedboat transfer to Krabi Town (approximately 90 minutes). Check in to your Krabi luxury accommodation. After settling in, visit the iconic Wat Tham Seua (Tiger Cave Temple) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for breathtaking panoramic views of Krabi's karst landscape
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Krabi Town's vibrant street food scene along Maharaj Road and the famous Walking Street Market. Sample local Krabi specialties — kanom jeen (fermented rice noodles with fish curry sauce), roti with banana and condensed milk, and fresh-squeezed sugarcane juice
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner cruise along the Krabi River estuary, gliding past mangroves, limestone cliffs, and traditional fishing villages. Premium dinner served on board with fresh seafood and Thai classics

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Phi Phi boutique hotel before departure — tropical smoothie bowls, granola, and fresh-brewed Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Street food lunch at Krabi Town's Chao Fa Walking Street — grilled pork skewers, pad thai from a wok stall, and fresh coconut pudding
meals.dinner: Sunset dinner cruise on the Krabi River — multi-course Thai seafood menu with grilled barramundi, red curry, and steamed jasmine rice; includes welcome cocktail

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Start no later than 08:30 to avoid midday heat. Krabi Town's Walking Street is most vibrant on Friday and Saturday evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour of the Four Islands (Koh Mor, Koh Tub, Koh Gai, and Koh Lading) departing from Ao Nang Beach. Snorkel the pristine reefs of Koh Lading, walk the stunning sandbar connecting Koh Tub and Koh Mor at low tide, and relax on secluded beaches
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through the sea caves and hidden lagoons of Ao Thalane — one of Krabi's most scenic kayaking destinations. Paddle through cathedral-like cave passages and emerge into secret enclosed lagoons surrounded by towering jungle-clad limestone walls
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang for dinner. Stroll the Ao Nang beachfront promenade and explore the lively evening market with street food stalls

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs benedict with smoked salmon, fresh tropical fruit, and cold-pressed green juice
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch on Koh Lading beach — premium bento boxes prepared by your tour operator with Thai sandwiches, fruits, and cold beverages
meals.dinner: Azzurra Restaurant, Ao Nang — upscale beachfront dining with panoramic sea views; signature grilled seafood platter and Thai-Italian fusion dishes

day_by_day.notes: The Four Islands sandbar is only accessible at low tide — confirm timing with your tour operator. Ao Thalane kayaking is best in the morning when waters are calmer; afternoon sessions are also available. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day private speedboat charter to Koh Hong Island Group — one of Krabi's most spectacular and less-visited destinations. Arrive at the secluded Hong Lagoon, accessible only through a narrow cave passage, and discover a hidden inland sea surrounded by jungle-covered cliffs
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Koh Hong archipelago — snorkel at the pristine reef gardens, relax on the white-sand beaches of Koh Pak Bia, and enjoy the exclusive atmosphere of these protected islands. Your private captain navigates to the best spots based on conditions
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi by late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening with a traditional Thai herbal steam bath and oil massage at your hotel spa, followed by a quiet dinner

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — congee with century egg and ginger, dim sum selection, and fresh watermelon juice
meals.lunch: Premium on-boat BBQ lunch at Koh Hong — grilled fresh catch, coconut rice, Thai salads, and cold tropical fruit; prepared by your private boat crew
meals.dinner: In-hotel fine dining — chef's tasting menu featuring southern Thai cuisine with Krabi-sourced ingredients; highlights include crab curry and stir-fried morning glory with oyster sauce

day_by_day.notes: Koh Hong is a protected national park — entry fees apply and visitor numbers are capped. Book your private speedboat charter at least 48 hours in advance. The lagoon cave passage requires swimming — a life jacket is provided.

day_by_day.morning: Rock climbing experience on Krabi's world-famous limestone karst cliffs at Railay Beach. A certified guide leads a half-day beginner to intermediate session on the stunning sea cliffs overlooking the Andaman Sea — no prior experience necessary
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Railay Beach's stunning peninsula — only accessible by boat — visiting Railay West, Railay East, Phra Nang Cave Beach (with its sacred princess cave), and the hidden Diamond Cave with its remarkable stalactite formations
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the Rayavadee Resort's Grotto Bar, dramatically set inside a natural limestone cave on Phra Nang Beach. One of Thailand's most unique bar experiences

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full American set with pancakes, bacon, eggs, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Railay Beach — The Last Bar restaurant for fresh seafood pasta, grilled fish, and cold beers with a beachfront view
meals.dinner: Rayavadee Resort's Raya Dining — one of Krabi's most prestigious restaurants; set in a pavilion surrounded by tropical gardens; four-course Thai degustation menu

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is accessible only by longtail boat from Ao Nang (15 minutes) or Krabi Town (45 minutes). Book rock climbing through a certified operator — Basecamp Tonsai or King Climbers are highly recommended. Phra Nang Cave Beach has a sacred shrine — dress respectfully.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer from Krabi to Koh Lanta (approximately 2 hours by ferry or 1.5 hours by speedboat). Check in to your Koh Lanta luxury resort. Spend the morning exploring Long Beach (Klong Dao) — one of Thailand's most pristine and uncrowded beaches with calm, clear waters
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the charming Old Town of Koh Lanta (Ban Si Raya) — a beautifully preserved wooden stilt village with Chinese-Thai heritage, colorful shophouses, artisan boutiques, and local cafes. Explore the seafront promenade and browse handmade crafts and local artwork
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Kantiang Bay — one of Koh Lanta's most secluded and scenic bays. Watch the sun dip below the Andaman horizon from a clifftop viewpoint, then descend to the beach for a romantic beachside dinner

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Krabi hotel before departure — French toast with local honey, fresh fruit salad, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Koh Lanta Old Town — seafood noodle soup at a traditional shophouse restaurant and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Pimalai Resort's Spice & Rice Restaurant, Kantiang Bay — sophisticated Thai cuisine in an open-air beachside setting; signature southern Thai yellow curry with fresh crab

day_by_day.notes: The speedboat transfer to Koh Lanta offers stunning views of the Krabi archipelago. Koh Lanta Old Town is best explored on foot or by bicycle — rent from your hotel. Kantiang Bay is a 45-minute drive from the main town — arrange transport through your resort.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling and diving day trip to the Koh Lanta Marine Park — home to some of Thailand's finest underwater ecosystems. Visit Koh Rok Nai and Koh Rok Nok, twin islands with extraordinary coral gardens, sea turtles, and leopard sharks. A private speedboat charter ensures exclusive access
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Hin Daeng and Hin Muang — two of Thailand's top dive sites, known for their dramatic underwater walls, manta ray sightings, and pelagic fish. Even non-divers can snorkel the shallower sections and witness spectacular marine life
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Enjoy a beachside sunset yoga session arranged by your resort, followed by a traditional Thai foot massage to ease the day's adventures

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast — energy-boosting smoothie bowls, granola with local honey, and scrambled eggs with herbs
meals.lunch: Beachside BBQ lunch on Koh Rok Nai — grilled seafood, steamed rice, fresh salads, and cold beverages prepared by your private boat crew
meals.dinner: Where Else? Bar & Restaurant, Koh Lanta — a beloved sunset spot with creative Thai fusion tapas, fresh seafood, and an impressive cocktail menu featuring local herbs and spirits

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok requires a national park entry fee. Hin Daeng and Hin Muang are advanced dive sites — snorkeling is available at surface level. Book through a certified dive operator. Manta ray sightings are more common between October and April.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Koh Lanta National Park by private guided tour — trek through primary rainforest to the park headquarters at the island's southern tip, spot monitor lizards, hornbills, and macaques, and visit the lighthouse with sweeping views of the Andaman Sea and surrounding islands
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely beach afternoon at Klong Nin Beach — a long, quiet stretch of golden sand with crystal-clear water and minimal crowds. Rent a beachside sun lounger and umbrella, swim in the calm sea, and enjoy a refreshing coconut on the beach
day_by_day.evening: Final evening on Koh Lanta — premium street food and night market experience at the Klong Dao Beach area. Sample the best of southern Thai street food: grilled whole fish with sweet chili sauce, kanom buang (crispy Thai crepes), and fresh durian for the adventurous

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — Thai-style morning spread with khao tom (rice soup), fried garlic eggs, fresh fruit, and Thai iced tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Time for Lime Restaurant, Klong Nin Beach — famous for its Thai cooking school and restaurant; fresh seafood salads, curries, and homemade ice cream
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Mango House, Koh Lanta — a beautifully restored colonial-era mansion with fine Thai cuisine, candlelit garden dining, and an excellent wine list; signature dish is the Mango House seafood curry

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta National Park charges a separate entry fee. The park trail can be muddy in October — wear sturdy footwear. Klong Nin Beach is approximately 20 minutes from the main town — arrange transport through your resort. Pack a bag for your final departure day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisurely breakfast at your resort. Take a last swim in the Andaman Sea and collect any remaining souvenirs from local boutiques near your hotel — handmade batik fabrics, Thai silk scarves, locally produced coconut products, and artisan jewelry make excellent keepsakes
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat or ferry transfer from Koh Lanta back to Krabi, then onward private transfer to Krabi International Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 3 hours from Koh Lanta to the airport to account for sea and road transfers
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Krabi International Airport — if flight timing allows, enjoy a final meal at the airport's premium lounge or a nearby restaurant en route

meals.breakfast: Final luxury resort breakfast — chef's special Thai breakfast set with coconut pancakes, fresh tropical fruit tower, and premium Thai coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Krabi Airport or en route — airport lounge dining or a quick stop at a quality Krabi Town restaurant for khao pad (Thai fried rice) and fresh spring rolls
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your speedboat or ferry departure time from Koh Lanta the evening before — schedules vary by season and sea conditions. Allow extra buffer time for the transfer chain: Koh Lanta pier → ferry/speedboat → Krabi pier → airport. Request a late checkout from your resort to maximize your final morning.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
